question.text: Which of the following best describes market risk as defined in the workbook?

answer.text: The risk of loss because a specific company's management makes poor business decisions
The risk that an investor cannot find a buyer for an illiquid asset
The risk of loss in value due to adverse price movements in assets traded at current market prices, such as equity, bonds, gold and real estate
The risk that the issuer of a debt instrument will default on interest or principal

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes market risk as the risk of loss in value because of adverse price movements in marketable investments such as equity, bonds, gold and real estate. Diversification and asset allocation are separately discussed as a way to manage business risk or decline in one or a few asset classes. The Trap: Company-specific management risk, illiquidity risk and credit/default risk are different risk categories. The "systematic vs unsystematic" labels and the claim that market risk cannot be diversified away are not used in this workbook section, so they should not be relied on here. Note: The workbook's market-risk definition and the related diversification/asset-allocation discussion are covered on pages 42, 43 and 45-46 of the NISM Series XVII Retirement Adviser Certification Examination workbook (June 2025, version 02).
